risk_modules.title: Heart Disease (WHO South Asia 10-Year CVD Risk)
risk_modules.methodology: Continuous South-Asia-calibrated 10-year cardiovascular & stroke risk model (ages 40–74) using lab-based total cholesterol or non-lab BMI.
risk_modules.why_it_matters: South Asians experience coronary artery disease and stroke roughly 5–10 years earlier than global averages, often with modest LDL cholesterol.

thresholds.skipped: Outside ages 40–74 (displays modifiable risk-factor count instead of guessed %)

recommended_tests: Fasting Lipid Profile (Total Chol, LDL, HDL, TG)
red_flags: Chest pain/pressure radiating to arm or jaw

risk_modules.title: BMI & Central Obesity (Indian Consensus Cutoffs)
risk_modules.methodology: Indian Consensus BMI (<18.5 underweight, 18.5–22.9 normal, 23.0–24.9 overweight, >=25.0 obese) paired with waist circumference (>=90 cm men, >=80 cm women).
risk_modules.why_it_matters: Indians accumulate higher visceral/abdominal fat at lower BMI ('thin-fat' phenotype), driving insulin resistance even when BMI looks borderline.

thresholds.low: BMI 18.5–22.9 kg/m² AND waist <90 cm (M) / <80 cm (F)
thresholds.high: BMI >= 25.0 kg/m² (obese) OR central obesity (waist >=90 cm M / >=80 cm F)

recommended_tests: Liver ultrasound / ALT if central obesity present
red_flags: Rapid unexplained weight gain with leg swelling or breathlessness (possible fluid retention)

risk_modules.title: Metabolic Syndrome (Harmonized South Asian Criteria)
risk_modules.methodology: Counts 5 cardiometabolic criteria: elevated waist (>=90M/80F), BP >=130/85, FPG >=100 mg/dL, Triglycerides >=150 mg/dL, low HDL (<40M/50F).
risk_modules.why_it_matters: Meeting >=3 of 5 criteria doubles 10-year cardiovascular risk and strongly predicts type 2 diabetes and fatty liver (MASLD).

thresholds.skipped: Skipped when fasting glucose, triglycerides, and HDL are all missing (never guessed)

red_flags: Co-existing chest discomfort, severe fatigue, or persistent hypertension >=180/120

risk_modules.title: Diabetes Risk (MDRF Indian Diabetes Risk Score)
risk_modules.methodology: Validated Indian screening score (0–100) combining age, waist circumference, physical activity, and parental diabetes history.
risk_modules.why_it_matters: Over 50% of Indians with early type 2 diabetes are asymptomatic; IDRS identifies high-risk individuals before complications begin.
modifiable_drivers: Daily physical activity (30–45 min brisk walking)
red_flags: Extreme thirst/urination with nausea, confusion, or glucose >400 / <54 mg/dL

risk_modules.title: Blood Pressure (ACC/AHA & Indian Hypertension Staging)
risk_modules.methodology: Stages systolic/diastolic BP into Normal (<120/80), Elevated (120–129/<80), Stage 1 (130–139 or 80–89), Stage 2 (>=140 or >=90), Crisis (>=180 or >=120).
risk_modules.why_it_matters: High blood pressure is the #1 modifiable driver of stroke, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease in India.

thresholds.high: Stage 2 (>=140 / >=90 mmHg) or Hypertensive Crisis (>=180 / >=120 mmHg)
thresholds.skipped: Requires positive systolic and diastolic BP

modifiable_drivers: Dietary sodium (<5 g salt/day; cut pickles & papad)
recommended_tests: Home BP log (morning & evening for 7 days)
red_flags: BP >=180/120 with headache, vision changes, chest pain, or weakness -> Call 112/108

risk_modules.title: Kidney Health (CKD-EPI 2021 Race-Free eGFR + Urine ACR)
risk_modules.methodology: KDIGO-aligned CKD-EPI 2021 race-free filtration equation (G1 >=90 to G5 <15 mL/min/1.73m²) combined with Urine ACR albuminuria staging (A1–A3).
risk_modules.why_it_matters: Diabetic and hypertensive kidney damage is silent until advanced; catching eGFR <60 or ACR >=30 early allows kidney-protective therapy.

thresholds.low: eGFR >= 60 mL/min/1.73m² AND Urine ACR < 30 mg/g (if tested)
thresholds.skipped: Requires serum creatinine lab value (never guessed)

red_flags: Sudden drop in urine output, severe leg/facial swelling, or breathlessness

faqs.title: Why South Asian BMI and waist cutoffs are stricter
faqs.summary: Indian consensus uses BMI >=23 for overweight and >=25 for obesity (instead of 25/30) because South Asians carry higher visceral fat at lower body weights.
faqs.answer: Indian Consensus Guidelines (Misra et al.) define BMI 18.5-22.9 kg/m2 as normal, 23.0-24.9 as overweight, and >=25.0 as obese. Central obesity is flagged at waist >=90 cm for men and >=80 cm for women because abdominal visceral fat drives insulin resistance, fatty liver, and early cardiovascular risk even at modest BMI.

faqs.title: Understanding CKD-EPI 2021 eGFR and Urine ACR
faqs.summary: CKD-EPI 2021 estimates kidney filtration without race adjustment; pairing eGFR with Urine ACR catches early diabetic or hypertensive kidney strain.
faqs.answer: Kidney risk uses both eGFR (G1 >=90, G2 60-89, G3a 45-59, G3b 30-44, G4 15-29, G5 <15 mL/min/1.73m2) and Urine ACR (A1 <30, A2 30-300, A3 >300 mg/g). Even with eGFR >=90, an ACR >=30 mg/g indicates early kidney stress that responds well to BP and sugar control.
